cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. This dripping tap is our chance to replace the whole sink. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only needs a washer. I've bought one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Excellent. We'll fit it while the sink's out and replace that swollen worktop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The worktop runs under every cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll empty the kitchen. With the cupboards out, we can finally fix the layout.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 worktop and A5 whole layout expand the fix, but A3 authority prefix gives little cooperative concession beyond using B washer.

relationship.evidence: B2 has bought a useful fix and B4 supplies structural scope, plausibly trying to limit work.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns the disruption warning into an opportunity for a full layout change.
